Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for New Zealand's response with the bat to get underway. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. Will Young and Devon Conway walk out to open the innings for the tourists. Blessing Muzarabani will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for Zimbabwe. Blesssing to Conway first up. Three slips, a gully and a short leg in place. Off we go...
... DAY 1, THIRD SESSION ...

The Zimbabwean pacers will need to take a leaf out of their Kiwi counterparts' book and stick to the basics, bowling around the off stump and maintaining consistent lines and lengths. New Zealand’s disciplined approach with the ball paid rich dividends, and if Zimbabwe are to make any inroads with the ball, their seamers will have to replicate that level of accuracy and patience. Back in a bit for the start of New Zealand's reply.

Apart from Taylor and Tsiga, the rest of the Zimbabwean batters let themselves down with their shot selection. After being 83/4 at one stage, the hosts capitulated following Taylor’s dismissal, though Tsiga did offer some late resistance. For New Zealand, Matt Henry set the tone with a probing opening spell, and it wasn’t long before Zakary Foulkes joined the act. The Kiwi bowlers made excellent use of the lateral movement on offer, consistently chipping away at the wickets to keep the pressure firmly on Zimbabwe. Henry finished with a well-deserved five-wicket haul, while Foulkes claimed four, underlining a dominant bowling display from the visitors.

A dismal showing with the bat from Zimbabwe! 125 marks their lowest score in this home season of Test cricket and with that, it’s time for TEA. On a wicket with less grass compared to the first Test and the steep bounce not as much, the hosts will be disappointed with their batting display. Brendan Taylor and Tafadzwa Tsiga demonstrated that the pitch wasn’t a minefield by any means. There were runs on offer for those willing to dig in and apply themselves.

OUT! GONE! CAUGHT! A special moment for debutant Matthew Fisher as he registers his maiden Test wicket! Hurls it full and in the channel of the off pole, getting a late away movement through the air. Tanaka Chivanga gets half-forward and tries to work that through covers, but fails to keep it along the ground, and ends up chipping it off the toe-end of the bat. The ball goes flat and dips towards Mitchell Santner at mid off. The Kiwi skipper gets low and snaffles the catch nicely. ZIMBABWE HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 125. And that will be an early Tea on Day 1.

The blueprint of New Zealand’s pace attack was quite simple. Pitch it persistently in and around off, and trust the ball to do the talking. Zakary Foulkes, on debut, followed the same script and was rewarded with the prized wicket of Sean Williams, deepening Zimbabwe’s troubles. At 43 for 3, the top order had already taken a significant hit. Hence, they couldn't keep the scorecard ticking along. And just as the partnership between skipper Ervine and Taylor was blossoming, Zakary Foulkes nicked Ervine off a beauty, which brought to a painful end for Zimbabwe in the first session. Zimbabwe’s priority will be to steady the ship and avoid a collapse, which has been their recurring vulnerability in this format. New Zealand, on the other hand, will look to build on their momentum and make further inroads into the batting lineup. Play resumes with the afternoon session starting at 10.40 am GMT. Stay tuned.

There hasn't been much steep bounce on offer, but the surface provided enough lateral movement to keep the batters honest. The occasional ball kicked awkwardly off a length, adding to the uncertainty. In the midst of it all, Brendan Taylor brought calm. He let the ball come to him, played with soft hands, and avoided anything extravagant. Welch supported him with a brief but valuable stand, before Henry removed him just before the drinks break.

It was a probing start for Zimbabwe’s batters, with New Zealand’s pacers operating like seasoned interrogators. Matt Henry struck in the third over, drawing Brian Bennett into a false stroke with a delivery that shaped away just enough. He nearly had two in two, but Will Young couldn’t hold on to a sharp chance at second slip of Nick Welch. Jacob Duffy complemented Henry well, maintaining a tight channel and letting the pitch do the rest.

SESSION SUMMARY - 28.1 Overs, 67 Runs, 4 Wickets. A very disappointing morning session for Zimbabwe as they have lost four big wickets. Zimbabwe’s batters managed to get a few starts, but none could carry on, barring Taylor, against New Zealand’s disciplined and controlled pace attack. The bowlers kept things simple, yet highly effective, and the dismissal of Craig Ervine right on the stroke of lunch added further pressure on the hosts.

Looks to drive it down the ground but there is just enough movement off the deck to catch the outside edge. It goes straight into the waiting hands of Will Young at second slip, who takes it at thigh height. Third catch for Young in the game already, and Ervine falls for 7 (28). Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going in Bulawayo with the sun shining in all its glory and not a cloud in the sky. Making a much-anticipated return to the international fold after nearly four years, Brendan Taylor walks out to open the innings alongside Brian Bennett. It is a symbolic second innings in Taylor’s international career, and adding to the emotion of the moment, his parents are in attendance to witness this special occasion. Matt Henry will open the attack for the Kiwis. Bennett to face the first ball. Three slips, a gully and a short leg in place. Here we go!

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford is near the deck. He shares that it's a beautiful day in Bulawayo, with the country slowly creeping into the summer months. Scott Styris joins him and informs that the surface for this Test is different from the previous one. Adds that it is a little drier and without much visible moisture. Scott believes it looks like a good wicket to bat on. Mentions that if the bounce remains consistent, there will be runs to be had. Overall, he expects the surface to play true, without too many deliveries taking off sharply due to the lack of moisture.

New Zealand head coach, Rob Walter, says the guys adapted well to the conditions and that they kept getting better and better. Stresses that it was good to see how their bowlers responded to the conditions. Highlights that they have come off a good T20 diet and were a bit on the aggressive side as well. Says they gave the guys an off for a couple of days for conditioning and had two really good training days as well. On the team combinations, he adds it's an exciting time for New Zealand cricket and Jacob Duffy has played for quite a while now, and he is excited to see him making his debut in the longest format. Shares losing Nathan Smith to injury was hard, but also points it is important to find the correct balance in the side and mentions that Zakary Foulkes has done well domestically, and Matthew Fisher has got some raw pace with him. From a bowling point of view, Rob stresses that if they can hit the right lengths consistently, it will be great. And batting-wise, he says they want to be patient and take their time in the middle. While in the field, Walter wants his men to tick all the boxes.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Will Young, Henry Nicholls, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Mitchell Santner (C), Zakary Foulkes (On debut) (In for Michael Bracewell), Matt Henry, Matthew Fisher (On debut) (In for Nathan Smith), Jacob Duffy (On debut) (In for Will O’Rourke).

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Brendan Taylor (In for Ben Curran), Nick Welch, Sean Williams, Craig Ervine (C), Sikandar Raza, Tafadzwa Tsiga(WK), Vincent Masekesa, Blessing Muzarabani, Tanaka Chivanga, Trevor Gwandu (In for Newman Nyamhuri).

The skipper of New Zealand, Mitchell Santner says that he would have bowled first as well. Feels that this is a better wicket compared to the last game. Mentions that there is less grass on the pitch but hopes there is still something in it early on for the pacers. Santner shares that it’s been good to enjoy a bit of downtime, but now it’s back to action mode after a couple of days of training. Informs that they have three debutants in Jacob Duffy, Zakary Foulkes and Matthew Fisher.

The captain of Zimbabwe, Craig Ervine, says the wicket looks a lot better with less grass. He expects it to play well this time around as compared to the last Test. On the learnings from the previous game, he says they will try to make improvements in all departments. Reflects that the guys have worked on specifics and are hopeful that they will be able to execute in the match. Informs two changes. Ben Curran makes way for Brendan Taylor and Newman Nyamhuri is out and Trevor Gwandu comes in for him.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.

In contrast, their opponents have some major injury concerns building into this Test match. Will O’Rourke is out with a back injury, and all-rounder Nathan Smith has an abdominal tear, which means that we are likely to see a couple of debutants for the visitors in this Test. Mitchell Santner will continue to lead the Kiwis in the second Test, as Tom Latham remains out of the team having failed to recover from a left shoulder injury. New Zealand beat Zimbabwe fairly dominantly in the last Test and have never lost a Test against the African nation. The Kiwis will aim to assert their dominance once again over a vulnerable Zimbabwean side, while the home side will look to show more grit and produce a much-improved performance. Stick around for the toss and team news.

The Chevrons will look forward to ending their poor streak in Test cricket and showcasing some good brand of cricket. And the return of Brendan Taylor, their fourth-highest Test run-getter, will be a big boost for Zimbabwe. The hosts will need to bring their A-game for the final match of this Test series and pose a challenge to the Kiwis. In the batting department, their experienced players like Craig Ervine, Sikandar Raza, Brendan Taylor, and Sean Williams hold the key on this Bulawayo pitch, where pacers had a major say in the first Test. Altogether, the hosts need a complete team effort to bounce back in this Test and finish this series on a level footing.
